result: Implemented focusa.mission_canvas.rich_host.launch through the canonical generated POST operation. Focusa Core now resolves and durably records one Desktop lifecycle projection for the exact Workstream, with idempotent lifecycle persistence and a durable event cursor; the API requires the generated Workstream command, explicit host permission/capability, and actor/authority context; Desktop uses registry-owned transport metadata and rejects foreign or stale lifecycle responses without forking or replacing Pi.

generated_contract.artifact_status: Canonical registry, OpenAPI path, generated TypeScript method, generated DTO, and generated validators remain parity-verified; no generated contract artifact was edited.

presentation_contract.surface_kind: Focusa Desktop Mission Canvas Svelte GUI tab
presentation_contract.canonical_runtime: Focusa Core and the existing Pi session remain canonical; Desktop is the rich projection host.
presentation_contract.eligible_contributions: Not applicable to host launch. The operation accepts no candidate contributions and never performs client-local eligibility or layout resolution.
presentation_contract.omitted_contribution_reasons: Not applicable to host launch; composition remains Core-owned by the existing projection resolver.

implementation: HostLifecycleLaunchCommand and HostLifecycleService validate WorkstreamContext, exact MissionCanvas scope, mission_canvas:host permission, host capability, and non-empty bounded idempotency before persistence.

The Core service resolves the Desktop renderer through the existing HostRendererResolutionService, derives one deterministic host instance for the complete scope, returns visible/focused HostLifecycleState, and records a scoped host_launched event without a Pi process id or Pi/model fork.

MissionCanvasStore atomically persists the lifecycle envelope and event, returns the original state for same-scope idempotency retries, increments lifecycle revision for a new command, and writes the durable event sequence into durable_event_cursor.

The API exposes the exact generated launch path separately from the legacy lifecycle adapter, extracts WorkstreamContext from explicit actor/authority headers, passes generated capabilities and permission projection to Core, and returns HostLifecycleState rather than a route-local document envelope.

MissionCanvasHttpTransport resolves method/path and control requirements from the generated operation registry, validates HostLifecycleState with generated validators, verifies outer and nested exact authority, and rejects foreign, malformed, stale revision, or stale cursor responses.

Hostile contract and Desktop runtime tests cover missing scope/idempotency, foreign Workstream and renderer authority, invalid host identity/state, stale lifecycle revision/cursor, generated POST/body/header ownership, no Pi fork fields, and preserved existing operation consumers.

negative_cases.foreign_workstream: Core exact scope validation rejects a foreign Workstream. Desktop validates both the outer HostLifecycleState authority and nested renderer resolution authority, rejecting foreign lifecycle scope before returning a response.
negative_cases.missing_authority: The API requires explicit x-focusa-actor-id and x-focusa-authority-ref for WorkstreamContext extraction; Desktop rejects missing generated Workstream authority before HTTP. Foreign Attachment, Continuity, WorkspaceBinding, RuntimeObject, and WorkSurface values do not become alternate owners.
negative_cases.stale_revision_cursor: The generated operation has no If-Match revision, but Desktop tracks HostLifecycleState lifecycle_revision and durable event cursor per exact authority and rejects regressions as stale_lifecycle_revision or stale_lifecycle_cursor. Core persistence uses revision-checked atomic updates.
negative_cases.unavailable_capability: HostLifecycleService delegates renderer capability selection to Core; absent Desktop and compatibility capabilities fail closed with capability_unavailable. Explicit Desktop capability selects focusa_desktop_tauri; the existing Pi renderer remains only an explicit compatibility fallback.
negative_cases.permission_denied: The state-aware API permission boundary and Core HostLifecycleService both require mission_canvas:host; missing permission cannot reach lifecycle persistence.
negative_cases.missing_idempotency: Generated transport rejects a missing idempotency_key before HTTP, and Core rejects blank or overlong keys before persistence. Same exact scope/key retries return the existing lifecycle state without a duplicate event.
negative_cases.empty_or_ineligible_contribution: Not applicable to launch: no contribution or layout input is accepted. The host operation neither invents content nor resolves composition; Core projection/recomposition remains the sole eligibility owner.
negative_cases.invalid_response: Generated HostLifecycleState validation plus bounded runtime checks reject invalid lifecycle enum values, host instance identity, missing durable cursor, missing nested renderer Workstream, and mismatched nested authority.
negative_cases.pi_continuity: The command carries the exact Workstream authority chain and no Pi process/session replacement field; Core records process_id as null and the transport/test path contains no child-process or fork behavior.

acceptance: Launches/presents Desktop for exact Workstream without forking Pi.
Uses POST /v1/mission-canvas/rich-host/launch and generated MissionCanvasClient.rich_hostLaunch with registry-owned method/path metadata.
